summary: Locked runner service account access due to Conditional Access policy during nightly gated release
description: Issue summary: During the 2026-03-12 nightly gated release, several CI jobs using the 'release-runner-us-east' service account failed to start. The pipeline stalled at 'Acquire runner' with 403/401-style authorization failures from the cloud IAM token exchange. Impact: Nightly release blocked for ~3.5 hours, manual rollback required for one canary. Environment: Production CI (self-hosted runners) in us-east region; release window 02:00-06:00 UTC. Affected components: ci-runner, auth, vault, gcp-iam. Steps to reproduce: 1) Trigger gated release pipeline targeting canary group. 2) Observe runner registration step hang and repeated auth errors in runner logs. 3) Attempt manual token refresh via ci-admin account fails with 'conditional access denied' response. Logs & observed errors: - Runner: "401: AccessDenied - ConditionalAccessPolicyRestrictsSignIn" - Token-service: "403 Forbidden: token exchange blocked by CA policy (require compliant device)" - Vault: "wrapped token unwrap succeeded" (no obvious Vault error) Notes: This appears related to a Conditional Access (CA) policy change that started enforcing device compliance for service principals earlier today. The release-runner service account uses short-lived OIDC tokens minted by the CI control plane; the policy may be evaluating the identity as a user session rather than a machine identity. No previous incidents observed for this runner pool.
comments: 2026-03-12 03:05 - Sophia Li (on-call SRE): Initial triage - runners failed to register; auth service returning CA-deny. Escalating to IAM team.
2026-03-12 03:18 - Ravi Patel (Release Eng): Confirmed pipeline blocked. We temporarily moved canary to earlier stable image to avoid user exposure. Need root cause before re-enabling nightlies.

2026-03-12 03:42 - Marcus Chen (IAM): Observed Conditional Access policy modification at 01:58 UTC that included a new 'require device_compliance' rule for service principals. Policy change came from SecOps request: 'tighten access for interactive sessions'.

2026-03-12 04:10 - Elena Gomez (Reporter): Note - release-runner identities authenticate via OIDC with audience claim 'ci-runner'. They do not surface a device_compliance signal. Suggest bypassing CA for this SP temporarily.
2026-03-12 05:05 - Marcus Chen (IAM): Applied temporary CA exclusion for service principal 'release-runner-sp' to restore flow. Nightly pipeline resumed. Need follow-up to define permanent fix.

2026-03-13 10:23 - Ravi Patel (Assignee): Investigation in progress - mapping where OIDC tokens are evaluated as user sessions. Drafting changes to token exchange to set 'auth_context' hint for machine identity.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Conditional Access policy treats any token exchange originating from the CI control plane as interactive because the exchange path includes a user-agent header from the webhook proxy.
Hypothesis B: New SecOps rule was applied broadly to service principals; vault-wrapped tokens lack the expected claim ('client_type':'machine') used by the CA gating logic.
Observed: Vault unwrap and local token caching succeeded; failure occurs on cloud IAM token mint step returning CA deny.
Correlation: Policy change timestamp aligns with start of failures. No code deploys to CI control plane during window.
Temporary mitigation: IAM applied an exclusion that restored runner auth but is not acceptable long-term. Need documented JIT exclusion and automation guardrails.

Next steps: 1) Define durable signal in OIDC token (e.g., add 'auth_method':'pod_identity' or 'client_type':'service') and coordinate with SecOps to map condition. 2) Harden CI token exchange to use dedicated mTLS channel for machine identities. 3) Add synthetic checks to detect CA policy regression before release windows.
resolution: Temporary workaround applied: SecOps added a scoped Conditional Access exclusion for the 'release-runner-sp' service principal and the nightly pipeline was resumed. Root cause: SecOps rollout of a device_compliance requirement inadvertently matched the CI token exchange path because tokens lacked a machine signal. Permanent fix plan: 1) Implement token claim augmentation in the CI token-minting service to include 'client_type':'machine' and 'auth_method':'oidc:ci' (PRs opened: infra#2418, ci#1192). 2) Coordinate with SecOps to map a CA condition that evaluates the new claim instead of blanket device_compliance. 3) Add pre-release synthetic gating that validates runner registration under current CA rules (task assigned to Release Eng). Follow-ups: update runbooks and add an automated rollback if CA changes block runner auth. Target completion: 2026-03-24.
workaround_steps: 1) SecOps: Add Conditional Access exclusion for 'release-runner-sp' (scoped to CI token exchange endpoints) to restore pipeline. (Already applied)
2) Release Eng: Avoid scheduling high-risk gated nightlies until claim augmentation is deployed.
3) SRE: Monitor runner registration metrics and alert on CA-deny spikes with a 1-minute window.
